title: Strawberry Begonia Varigata - Saxifraga Stolonifera - 1x Mini Plug Plant
description:
Plant:
 
 Strawberry Begonia / Creeping Saxifrage
 

  Botanical name:
 
  Saxifraga stolonifera
 
 (syn.
 
  Saxifraga sarmentosa
 
 )
 

  Origin:
 
 Japan, China, Korea


 Key features

  Not a true strawberry or begonia; common name refers to leaf shape and pink-tinged foliage.
 

  Forms a low, spreading plant and produces
  
   runners (stolons)
  
  with
  
   plantlets
  
  that can be potted on.
 

  May produce
  
   small white flowers
  
  on upright spikes in summer.
 

  If grown outdoors in the UK,
  
   slugs/snails may damage
  
  foliage.
 

 Care (quick guide)

   Light:
  
  Bright,
  
   indirect
  
  light; avoid strong direct sun (can scorch). East- or north-facing window suits well.
 

   Water:
  
  Let the
  
   top third of the compost dry
  
  before watering again.
  
    Crispy leaves = often too dry
   

    Yellow/rotting lower leaves = often too wet
   


   Soil:
  
  Free-draining mix (e.g., fern/houseplant mix with added
  
   perlite/pumice
  
  ; optional fine sand).
 

   Humidity:
  
  Average household humidity is fine; higher humidity helps.
 

   Temperature:
  
  Approx.
  
   10–32°C
  
  ; avoid consistently below
  
   8°C
  
  .
 

   Feeding:
  
  During growth, feed about
  
   every 4th watering
  
  ; reduce to
  
   every 6th
  
  in autumn/winter.
 

   Pets:
  
  Generally considered
  
   pet-safe
  
  , but ingestion isn’t recommended.
